authorities.authority: OpenStax, Rice University, University Physics Volume 2
authorities.locator: 13.1 Faraday's Law, magnetic-flux definition, equation 13.1, and SI-unit paragraph
observed: The learning objective specifies the angle between the surface normal and magnetic field.
Equation 13.1 defines magnetic flux by a surface integral of the dot product of the magnetic field and the unit normal.
The text identifies magnetic flux as the quantity used in Faraday's induction law and identifies Michael Faraday.
The magnetic-flux unit is the weber, equivalent to tesla times square meter.
authorities.use: Supports the angle-to-normal definition, normal-component interpretation, units and scientist identity. No external example, exercise, answer, numerical constant or extra formula is imported into n124.

authorities.authority: Feynman, Leighton and Sands, The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Caltech
authorities.locator: Volume II, 3-2 The flux of a vector field; 3-3 first two cube faces
observed: Flux is the surface integral of the normal component of a vector field; the definition also applies to an open surface.
The first cube face has the negative of the field's x component as its outward flux contribution; the opposite face has a positive contribution.
authorities.use: Supports the signed normal-component meaning of flux. The outward-normal convention of a closed surface is not imposed on this open plane-loop surface.

reviewerInference.scope: p0307#10 read with the unchanged definitions in p0307#4+p0307#7 and p0307#8
reasoning: The lesson's unchanged cosine formula permits negative flux when the field points against the chosen normal.
Reversing the selected normal changes the sign of the normal component and of flux, without changing the geometrical field-line crossings.
Normalizing line density on a unit area perpendicular to the field does not assign a sign to crossings.
In this uniform-field, planar case, an unsigned geometrical count under the density convention represents the flux magnitude; signed flux requires a directed count relative to the chosen normal.
reviewerInference.classification: Independent physics reasoning, not an observed source glyph, figure fact, translation-derived premise or answer-key calculation.
